target.title: fix(codex): bound app-server websocket handshake waits to requestTimeoutMs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators using Codex app-server over websocket/unix transport would hang forever on initialize/RPC when a peer accepted the socket but never completed the WebSocket upgrade.

## Why This Change Was Made

Bound upgrades with `ws.handshakeTimeout` **and** an explicit CONNECTING deadline at the transport chokepoint (`createWebSocketTransport`). `ws.handshakeTimeout` alone does **not** abort custom `createConnection` (Unix) upgrades — verified with a never-upgrade unix peer that stayed CONNECTING past the library timeout.

Production budget is resolved `appServer.requestTimeoutMs` (default 60s) from `CodexAppServerClient.start` via `resolveCodexAppServerRuntimeOptions()` — not a competing fixed handshake policy and not a new config key.

Short `handshakeTimeoutMs` overrides remain test/proof-only hang floors.

**Landing-unit split (ClawSweeper maintainer option 1):** APNs raw-socket CodeQL allowlist is **not** in this PR. That security-boundary classification lives in sibling [#109357](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/109357). This head is Codex transport only (3 files).

**Timeout contract (ClawSweeper recommended option):** reuse existing resolved `requestTimeoutMs` as the single request + upgrade budget for TCP and Unix. No distinct handshake config surface.

Collision check: overlapping [#108795](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/108795) was closed unmerged; this PR remains the complete TCP+Unix candidate. APNs allowlist split to [#109357](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/109357).

## User Impact

- **Before:** never-upgrade peers hang initialize/RPC forever (TCP and Unix).
- **After:** handshake follows operator `requestTimeoutMs` (default 60s) on both TCP and Unix, then emits transport exit (`1006`).

## Evidence

Exact head: `3624728aba1b78d46711d2026bc1bfc40848aefb`

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/transport-websocket.test.ts -- --run --reporter=verbose
```

```text
node=v22.22.0
head=3624728aba1b78d46711d2026bc1bfc40848aefb

[codex handshake negative control] outcome=still-pending readyState=0 wait_ms=300 without_handshakeTimeout=true
[codex handshake proof] timed_out=true elapsed_ms=200 code=1006 handshakeTimeout_ms=200 production_ms=60000
[codex handshake tcp non-default] timed_out=true elapsed_ms=250 code=1006 handshakeTimeout_ms=250
[codex handshake unix non-default] timed_out=true elapsed_ms=251 code=1006 handshakeTimeout_ms=250
[codex handshake initialize proof] timed_out=true elapsed_ms=200 message=initialize transport failed after request write: WebSocket was closed before the connection was established

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  7 passed (7)
```

Current-`main` negative: without this patch, a peer that accepts TCP/Unix but never upgrades leaves `ws` in `CONNECTING` (readyState=0) with no exit — same as the executable negative control above (`without_handshakeTimeout=true`, still-pending after 300ms). After fix: production transport paths emit `1006` within the supplied handshake budget.

## Verification

- Exact head: `3624728aba1b78d46711d2026bc1bfc40848aefb`
- Files vs `main`: `client.ts`, `transport-websocket.ts`, `transport-websocket.test.ts` only (zero CodeQL / APNs diff)
- `oxfmt --check` on touched files — passed
- `git diff --check` — passed
- Focused tests: 7 passed
- Mutation / negative control: raw `ws` without timeout stays CONNECTING; fixed transport exits `1006`

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: stalled WebSocket upgrade no longer wedges Codex app-server initialize/RPC forever.
Real environment tested: local loopback never-upgrade TCP + Unix peers; production entry points `createWebSocketTransport` and `CodexAppServerClient.initialize`.
Exact commands run: see Evidence.
Observed output after fix: see Evidence paste.
Evidence:
- Negative control proves unbounded CONNECTING without a handshake budget
- TCP and Unix production paths honor non-default budgets (~250ms measured)
- Initialize fails closed when handshake never completes
What was not tested: live remote Codex app-server / real outage; full 60s production wait (tests use short floors; production_ms=60000 asserted as the default constant)

## Risk / Compatibility

Medium (availability/timeout policy, intentional). A legitimate upgrade slower than `appServer.requestTimeoutMs` now exits `1006` instead of waiting forever. Mitigation: reuse the existing operator-visible request timeout (default 60s); no new config key. Security-boundary risk removed from this landing unit via [#109357](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/109357).

AI-assisted: yes (Cursor).
